CHANGED.issue: useSessionKey requires msg.sender == owner, but dApp should call this method on behalf of user (via EntryPoint or SmartAccount). Entire session key module is broken.
CHANGED.proposed_solution: Add authorizedCallers mapping to allow owner to specify which smart accounts can use session keys
CHANGED.verification: Current code at lines 179-203 in SessionKeyModule.sol shows the restrictive check - the fix is NOT implemented
edge_cases_missed: The proposed solution in the document contains a logical error: it keeps the original 'if (msg.sender != key.owner) revert Unauthorized();' check and then adds a nested check that can never execute (since msg.sender would have already been rejected if not equal to key.owner)
No mechanism to prevent front-running where an attacker could quickly call setAuthorizedCaller before a legitimate transaction
No event emitted when authorized caller is added/removed for monitoring suspicious activity
CHANGED.simpler_alternative: Replace the simple owner check with: require(caller == key.owner || authorizedCallers[key.owner][caller], "Unauthorized");
CHANGED.gas_impact: ~3K gas for mapping lookup (cheaper than current approach which always reverts for legitimate use cases) + 1 storage slot per authorized mapping entry

CHANGED.issue: setP256Verifier can be called instantly by owner, allowing malicious verifier installation if owner key is compromised (e.g., setting MockP256 that accepts any proof)
CHANGED.proposed_solution: Add timelock with pending state: setP256Verifier() sets pending value, confirmP256Verifier() executes after 48h delay
CHANGED.verification: Current code at lines 122-128 in SocialRecoveryModule.sol shows simple setter without timelock - the fix is NOT implemented
edge_cases_missed: No way to cancel a pending verifier update if needed (e.g., if owner realizes they proposed a malicious address)
Should consider emitting a warning event when timelock starts so community can monitor for suspicious activity
Fixed 48h timelock may not be appropriate for all chains/network conditions (might be too long for urgent fixes on some L2s)
CHANGED.simpler_alternative: Could use OpenZeppelin's TimelockController but would be overkill for this single-variable use case
CHANGED.gas_impact: ~5K gas (2 storage writes) + 2 storage slots for pending values

CHANGED.issue: setProviderStatus allows invalid state transitions like ACTIVE→SUNSET (skipping DEPRECATED), risking UserOp fund loss when EntryPoint deposits are lost
CHANGED.proposed_solution: Add state machine validation: ACTIVE→only DEPRECATED, DEPRECATED→only SUNSET, SUNSET→terminal state
CHANGED.verification: Current code at lines 40-45 in TrustProviderRegistry.sol shows no transition validation - the fix is NOT implemented
edge_cases_missed: Doesn't explicitly forbid UNREGISTERED→DEPRECATED/SUNSET transitions (though these are already prevented by ProviderNotRegistered check)
No consideration for emergency bypass mechanism if governance is compromised and immediate SUNSET is needed
Could add more detailed revert messages to help frontend applications handle specific transition errors
CHANGED.simpler_alternative: Could just block the specific ACTIVE→SUNSET transition instead of implementing full state machine
CHANGED.gas_impact: ~200 gas for additional branching checks - negligible

CHANGED.issue: Single failed transfer in batch causes entire batch to revert, denying funds to all recipients (e.g., one blacklisted address blocks 200 others)
CHANGED.proposed_solution: Implement pull pattern: track individual failures, continue processing, leave failed amounts in treasury for later recovery
CHANGED.verification: Current code at lines 140-148 in Treasury.sol still reverts on any transfer failure - the fix is NOT implemented
edge_cases_missed: Using low-level token.call() instead of safeTransfer() introduces risk with non-standard ERC20 tokens that return boolean values unconventionally
No mechanism to prevent dust attacks via many tiny failed transactions that could grief the system
Should consider minimum amount thresholds or failure rate limits to prevent spam
CHANGED.simpler_alternative: Full pull pattern where users claim funds would be more robust but significantly more complex and UX-intensive
CHANGED.gas_impact: ~500 gas per failed transfer + 1 event; storage efficient as amounts are zeroed after processing attempt

NEW.proposal: Instead of authorizedCallers mapping, use ERC-1271 signature validation to allow smart accounts to prove ownership of the key
NEW.rationale: More standardized approach that doesn't require owner to pre-authorize each smart account; follows account abstraction principles
NEW.tradeoffs: More complex verification logic (requires checking if caller is a contract and calling isValidSignature), but more flexible and standards-compliant

NEW.proposal: Add a centralized emergency pause mechanism governed by multisig that can temporarily halt critical functions (like setP256Verifier, setProviderStatus) across all modules when attacks are detected
NEW.rationale: Provides defense-in-depth; individual fixes prevent specific attacks but a circuit breaker protects against unknown or combined attack vectors
NEW.tradeoffs: Adds centralization risk and complexity, but could be designed to require multiple signatures and automatic expiration
